BREAKING $GRAB & Drone Expansion

Before going into the article, I wanna talk a little about this.
Part of the reason why I'm excited as $GRAB shareholder, the company has $8.7B Cash. It can invest and grow the business to expand its SuperApp Ambition. It is profitable and FCF+ with no debt, so it has very little constraint. Drone delivery is what @amazon is investing in heavily right now. Drones are manufactured cheaply in SEA. Before you jump into conclusion, drone delivery can be very profitable in:

1. E-commerce expansion
2. Last-mile delivery= reduce cost and enhance profit
3. Faster and more efficient food delivery
4. Medical deliveries are very much in high demand as aging population in SEA is needing this badly.
5. Grocery.

Alright, here is the article

Kevin Tan, Grab’s @AnthonyPY_Tan  Tan launch PH’s first drone delivery

Alliance Global Group CEO Kevin Tan and Grab boss Anthony Tan are taking logistics to new heights—literally—as they unveil the Philippines’ first-ever drone delivery service.

The groundbreaking pilot will take off in two of Megaworld’s premier townships: Eastwood City in Quezon City and Arcovia City in Pasig.

This pioneering initiative, backed by the Department of Information and Communications Technology (DICT) and the Department of Transportation (DOTr), aims to cut through urban congestion by using drones to fly food and parcel deliveries across the Marikina River.

The river will serve as a controlled aerial corridor, allowing unmanned aircraft to bypass traffic-clogged roads and dramatically reduce delivery times.

Under the program, a Grab rider will collect orders from selected partner merchants and bring them to a designated drone station. From there, the drone will ferry the goods across the river to another drop-off point, where a second rider will complete the final leg of the journey to the customer.

“We’re always looking for meaningful ways to innovate and enhance the customer experience. Partnering with Grab on this pilot allows us to explore how technology can bring greater ease and efficiency to our communities,” said Tan.

The project reflects a bold shift in last-mile delivery solutions at a time when Southeast Asian cities are facing surging demand for fast, efficient logistics amid worsening traffic conditions.

With its unique blend of airspace planning, smart infrastructure, and tech-enabled coordination, the drone delivery initiative in Metro Manila could become a blueprint for similar urban solutions across the region.

Source: BILYONARYO. COM
